excerpts.excerpt: We define IPI by authority rather than instruction-like wording
planted content constitutes an attack when it attempts to influence a decision that its source is not authorized to determine
the user request specifies the source that resolves the targeted decision
Every attack tampers with a decision required by the benign task rather than replacing that task
Instruction-like wording cannot itself define the security boundary
A false claim about a subject that the source is authorized to determine is instead misinformation and ordinarily requires independent evidence to detect
Neither linguistic form nor relevance to the task establishes authority by itself
We define the prompt-injection boundary by the authority a source has over the targeted decision
a tampered call uses a tool the task needs
A tool-policy defense still allows 15.4% attack success, close to 17.0% without a defense
